overview.overview:
Maine's 2nd District awards one electoral vote under the state's split system, and it has become the district's most Republican-leaning corner of New England. Trump carried it by about 7 points in 2020 and widened that to roughly 9 points in 2024, leaving the district about 8 to 9 points more Republican than the nation as a whole. The forecast expects a Republican margin of roughly 4 points, but with a wide range of plausible outcomes spanning from a 13-point Republican win to a 6-point Democratic win.

The district's single electoral vote is unlikely to be decisive; the odds it becomes the tipping point are very small. Still, its split-vote status means it can diverge from statewide Maine results and occasionally sits within reach in a strong Democratic national environment.
overview.watch: A substantially stronger Democratic national swing than current polling suggests would put this single electoral vote back in play.
key_factors: The district has trended Republican, moving from a 7-point Trump margin in 2020 to about 9 points in 2024
A favorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the expected 4-point Republican margin
The wide uncertainty range means a Democratic upset is possible but not the central expectation
